segment:
She wished it was still Christmas; it was more real than this.

“Did you want to walk home alone?”

The voice came out of the dark next to her without warning, and Mara jumped. He had spoken softly but deliberately. The words did not echo in her head with his usual cadence. They sounded like something that had come to him as a surprise, even as he was saying it. She felt her face turning bright red under her cap. She looked for the lights on the street, but they were far back, and there were too many shadows, too many angles on the sidewalk. She tried to think of an answer that would not give him the power to say the things she didn’t want to hear. She knew he could smell her hesitation on the air between them. “I didn’t think about it,” she said finally. “I usually go with you.”

His eyes were very close to her as if they had moved closer at the sound of her voice. Mara turned away from him again, trying to find a little space between them in the dark. She heard him sigh softly. He said something that she couldn’t understand. The sound was like an engine in a dark garage. He was very near again, almost breathing on her face as if he had moved closer while she wasn’t looking. His hand touched her arm gently, but his touch was very warm for someone who had been out in the cold for so long. “You’re a lot more attractive than I am,” she said to fill in the empty space between them. “I know I’m not supposed to say that,” she added quickly. “But you can hear it anyway.”

“I don’t think you’re trying to make me feel bad,” he said after a moment. His voice was low and steady, and she wondered how he had heard her at all. “You just want to say something, and I didn’t hear it.” He moved closer, and she felt a sudden pressure on the inside of her thigh from his fingertips. Mara tried to move away, but the sidewalk was slippery where they had been walking for so long. She felt his warmth against her side, and her heart was beating so fast she thought she would pass out. He turned his face away from her, and she could feel him breathing on her ear. She shivered in the cold air and wished she could feel a breeze. She took a few slow breaths. His hand was still touching her leg, and she couldn’t hear anything else because of the pounding in her chest.

segment:
She didn’t remember taking off the cross. A knot of tension in her stomach started to release.
She looked up at the dark buildings and heard rain falling again. There was not enough wind to move it sideways. She lifted her head toward the sound of the water. They passed a lamppost, and she noticed his hand reaching toward her. He hesitated a second and moved toward her. Mara looked down at his palm outstretched to hers and raised her own hand into his. It felt warm and solid. She didn’t let go.

After another block Jonah put his other arm around her shoulder. He stopped walking and looked at her. She did not move, but her mouth fell open in surprise. She thought he might kiss her, and she remembered their first kiss at the cafe. He was leaning down toward her, but before he touched her he looked at her again. A single raindrop slid off his eyelid down onto his cheek. Her lips felt very warm and moist. She wanted to kiss him, and she wanted him to want to kiss her. She closed her eyes and turned her head. She heard his breath on her neck and felt him lean away. The hand at her back went limp for a second before lifting away completely. They started walking again without words.

After a few steps she felt his fingers brush her hair. He stopped, but she didn’t. Then he caught up with her and put his arm around her again. This time she turned and saw him coming toward her. He reached past her cheekbone down to the side of her neck. She felt a hard muscle under his skin. His breath on her neck made her want to push herself closer to him. He was not moving, but she closed her eyes and turned toward him. Her mouth opened and she touched his shoulder. He didn’t pull away from her. A hard knot formed in her stomach again. She turned her head back and tasted salt. She closed her eyes again, and he moved slowly down her neck and pressed her chest into himself. He stopped at her collarbone, but she did not feel pain. The hand at her waist moved up and touched the back of her head. She put her hand against his chest and felt it moving in and out with her breathing. The wetness on her lips tasted like blood. She opened her mouth and let the salt trickle into her mouth.

segment:
Mara knew Jonah would offer to get her a taxi. She did not want one. She had learned the city. She had learned it was safe here if she stayed alert. She could walk from Fulcrum to her apartment in an hour and ten minutes. The walk would let her think. She could not think during work. She needed a way to recover, even though recovery might make things worse.

Mara did not need Jonah to stay with her, either. She did not want him to. Her first impulse was to say good night and go. But if he asked where she would go, she did not know how to answer. If he offered to get her a taxi or walk her home, she would say no. He might press his questions until she had no choice but to lie.

She thought about what a lie would cost her. It was impossible to keep one secret from him, even when she had tried. She did not know how she could hide the others. The lies and the secrets made everything worse. He had asked if she ever trusted him. Her answer was no.

Jonah stopped walking and looked back. “Are you all right?” he asked.

Mara saw the crease between his eyes again and wanted to touch it. She wanted to hold his hand, too. He stood looking at her like a man who wanted her to take something, as if there were something inside him that belonged to her, but he did not know how to give it to her.

She said, “I’m sorry I was cold tonight. I shouldn’t have let it get to me.”

“It wasn’t your fault,” he said.

She said, “We have an agreement that I’ll tell you if something goes wrong at Fulcrum. But it’s also important to me to keep my word, and not make false reports. If we’re going to have an agreement, it has to be mutual.”

He took a step closer to her, so that their shoulders touched. She looked at him. Her hair covered her face. The scent of his shirt covered her. She breathed the same air he did. This was not a safe distance from him. But she felt safe, here, with him.

She put out her hand. He took it. “If you don’t trust me enough to ask for help, how can I trust you?” he said.

“You can trust me if you let me go.”

He did not let go of her hand. “You would have gotten hurt at Fulcrum.”

She knew that was a true thing. She said it to herself.

He said, “I don’t know what I would do if anything happened to you.”

segment:
She didn’t remember taking off the cross. A knot of tension in her stomach started to release.
She looked up at the dark buildings and heard cars in the distance. The weight of what she had done was slowly lifting. The long afternoon had seemed like a nightmare. They had passed from one scenario to another without pause, testing her strength of will. She could hear herself protesting as Jonah pressed her closer, trying to get her to act as the target instead of the subject. For the first time she saw him as an enemy. But just before he took the cross, she lost it. He did not take the cross, and she had done nothing to stop him. She had acted as a puppet on his string.
The silence stretched out between them. Finally, his arm brushed against hers, and she looked up. The streetlights gave a glow to the street that made his eyes bright and clear.
“Come.” His voice was soft but strong. It sent a vibration through her body. She turned to look at him but didn’t move. His hand reached out to her, palm open. “We are done.”
She took a step back. The last memory of Fulcrum and Jonah made her sick inside. He still seemed like the enemy, not the friend she had come to depend on. She tried to speak but couldn’t. He watched her and waited for her to find her voice.
“I don’t know what to do with you,” she whispered. She stepped back. The light disappeared behind him and showed her just his silhouette.
“Then why are you here?” he asked. She could hear the hurt in his voice, even through the rain.
She turned away from him and watched the lights of the cars passing on the road. She didn’t want to go back to the apartment and face another day of what this had become. She felt as if she was losing control of her mind and body. “I don’t know.”
“So what are you waiting for?”
Mara looked away from the lights and turned back toward Jonah. She tried not to think of what had happened and focused on what she felt in her body. Her skin was wet and cold, but inside, a fire was still burning. It made her feel alive and powerful. “I don’t want to go home.”
He nodded slowly, as if he understood. She couldn’t remember how she got into his bed last time, and she didn’t want to remember. She had lost everything in the rush of what happened. If she was going to get through this night, she needed to think differently about what she wanted. She thought about how much she valued her control over her own body. It had always been an important part of her identity. She thought of the way he had made her feel small and powerless during their session. The feelings that she felt in his presence scared her.

It felt warm and solid. She didn’t let go.

After another block Jonah put his other arm around her shoulder. He stopped walking and looked at her. She did not move, but her mouth fell open in surprise. She thought he might kiss her, and she remembered their first kiss at the cafe. He was leaning down toward her, but before he touched her he looked at her again. A single raindrop slid off his eyelid down onto his cheek. Her lips felt very warm and moist. She wanted to kiss him, and she wanted him to want to kiss her. She closed her eyes and turned her head. She heard his breath on her neck and felt him lean away. The hand at her back went limp for a second before lifting away completely. They started walking again without words.

After a few steps she felt his fingers brush her hair. He stopped, but she didn’t. Then he caught up with her and put his arm around her again. This time she turned and saw him coming toward her. He reached past her cheekbone down to the side of her neck. She felt a hard muscle under his skin. His breath on her neck made her want to push herself closer to him. He was not moving, but she closed her eyes and turned toward him. Her mouth opened and she touched his shoulder. He didn’t pull away from her. A hard knot formed in her stomach again. She turned her head back and tasted salt. She closed her eyes again, and he moved slowly down her neck and pressed her chest into himself. He stopped at her collarbone, but she did not feel pain. The hand at her waist moved up and touched the back of her head. She put her hand against his chest and felt it moving in and out with her breathing. The wetness on her lips tasted like blood. She opened her mouth and let the salt trickle into her mouth.

segment:
Mara knew Jonah would offer to get her a taxi. She did not want one. She had learned the city. She had learned it was safe here if she stayed alert. She could walk from Fulcrum to her apartment in an hour and ten minutes. The walk would let her think. She could not think during work. She needed a way to recover, even though recovery might make things worse.

Mara did not need Jonah to stay with her, either. She did not want him to. Her first impulse was to say good night and go. But if he asked where she would go, she did not know how to answer. If he offered to get her a taxi or walk her home, she would say no. He might press his questions until she had no choice but to lie.

She thought about what a lie would cost her. It was impossible to keep one secret from him, even when she had tried. She did not know how she could hide the others. The lies and the secrets made everything worse. He had asked if she ever trusted him. Her answer was no.

Jonah stopped walking and looked back. “Are you all right?” he asked.

Mara saw the crease between his eyes again and wanted to touch it. She wanted to hold his hand, too. He stood looking at her like a man who wanted her to take something, as if there were something inside him that belonged to her, but he did not know how to give it to her.

She said, “I’m sorry I was cold tonight. I shouldn’t have let it get to me.”

“It wasn’t your fault,” he said.

She said, “We have an agreement that I’ll tell you if something goes wrong at Fulcrum. But it’s also important to me to keep my word, and not make false reports. If we’re going to have an agreement, it has to be mutual.”

He took a step closer to her, so that their shoulders touched. She looked at him. Her hair covered her face. The scent of his shirt covered her. She breathed the same air he did. This was not a safe distance from him. But she felt safe, here, with him.

She put out her hand. He took it. “If you don’t trust me enough to ask for help, how can I trust you?” he said.

“You can trust me if you let me go.”

He did not let go of her hand. “You would have gotten hurt at Fulcrum.”

She knew that was a true thing. She said it to herself.

He said, “I don’t know what I would do if anything happened to you.”

segment:
She wished it was still Christmas; it was more real than this.

“Did you want to walk home alone?”

The voice came out of the dark next to her without warning, and Mara jumped. He had spoken softly but deliberately. The words did not echo in her head with his usual cadence. They sounded like something that had come to him as a surprise, even as he was saying it. She felt her face turning bright red under her cap. She looked for the lights on the street, but they were far back, and there were too many shadows, too many angles on the sidewalk. She tried to think of an answer that would not give him the power to say the things she didn’t want to hear. She knew he could smell her hesitation on the air between them. “I didn’t think about it,” she said finally. “I usually go with you.”

His eyes were very close to her as if they had moved closer at the sound of her voice. Mara turned away from him again, trying to find a little space between them in the dark. She heard him sigh softly. He said something that she couldn’t understand. The sound was like an engine in a dark garage. He was very near again, almost breathing on her face as if he had moved closer while she wasn’t looking. His hand touched her arm gently, but his touch was very warm for someone who had been out in the cold for so long. “You’re a lot more attractive than I am,” she said to fill in the empty space between them. “I know I’m not supposed to say that,” she added quickly. “But you can hear it anyway.”

“I don’t think you’re trying to make me feel bad,” he said after a moment. His voice was low and steady, and she wondered how he had heard her at all. “You just want to say something, and I didn’t hear it.” He moved closer, and she felt a sudden pressure on the inside of her thigh from his fingertips. Mara tried to move away, but the sidewalk was slippery where they had been walking for so long. She felt his warmth against her side, and her heart was beating so fast she thought she would pass out. He turned his face away from her, and she could feel him breathing on her ear. She shivered in the cold air and wished she could feel a breeze. She took a few slow breaths. His hand was still touching her leg, and she couldn’t hear anything else because of the pounding in her chest.

segment:
She didn’t remember taking off the cross. A knot of tension in her stomach started to release.
She looked up at the dark buildings and heard cars in the distance. The weight of what she had done was slowly lifting. The long afternoon had seemed like a nightmare. They had passed from one scenario to another without pause, testing her strength of will. She could hear herself protesting as Jonah pressed her closer, trying to get her to act as the target instead of the subject. For the first time she saw him as an enemy. But just before he took the cross, she lost it. He did not take the cross, and she had done nothing to stop him. She had acted as a puppet on his string.
The silence stretched out between them. Finally, his arm brushed against hers, and she looked up. The streetlights gave a glow to the street that made his eyes bright and clear.
“Come.” His voice was soft but strong. It sent a vibration through her body. She turned to look at him but didn’t move. His hand reached out to her, palm open. “We are done.”
She took a step back. The last memory of Fulcrum and Jonah made her sick inside. He still seemed like the enemy, not the friend she had come to depend on. She tried to speak but couldn’t. He watched her and waited for her to find her voice.
“I don’t know what to do with you,” she whispered. She stepped back. The light disappeared behind him and showed her just his silhouette.
“Then why are you here?” he asked. She could hear the hurt in his voice, even through the rain.
She turned away from him and watched the lights of the cars passing on the road. She didn’t want to go back to the apartment and face another day of what this had become. She felt as if she was losing control of her mind and body. “I don’t know.”
“So what are you waiting for?”
Mara looked away from the lights and turned back toward Jonah. She tried not to think of what had happened and focused on what she felt in her body. Her skin was wet and cold, but inside, a fire was still burning. It made her feel alive and powerful. “I don’t want to go home.”
He nodded slowly, as if he understood. She couldn’t remember how she got into his bed last time, and she didn’t want to remember. She had lost everything in the rush of what happened. If she was going to get through this night, she needed to think differently about what she wanted. She thought about how much she valued her control over her own body. It had always been an important part of her identity. She thought of the way he had made her feel small and powerless during their session. The feelings that she felt in his presence scared her.
